drivers.name: Atlona OmniStream
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Atlona OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the Telnet CLI (port 23). Supports source routing, audio mute/volume, video enable, HDCP, analog speaker power, and CEC/RS-232 display triggers. Runtime control surface only — install-time setup is configured in the device's web UI.

help.overview: Atlona OmniStream is an AV-over-IP encoder/decoder system. Encoders take HDMI sources and produce network streams; decoders pick a stream and output HDMI to a display. Routing happens by setting which IP stream each decoder receives (the VideoInput command).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the OmniStream unit via its web UI. 2. In the web UI, disable Telnet login authentication (IPLogin) so
   this driver can connect without credentials.
3. Configure encoder sessions (multicast addresses, video format)
   and decoder IP inputs in the web UI before driver use.
4. Connect this driver to port 23. The HDMI output index ranges
   1..2 on most decoders; the session index ranges 1..6.
5. Volume range is 0..15 (Atlona's native scale). 6. To route a source: send the "Set Video Input" command with the
   output number and the IP input name (e.g. "ip_input3") configured
   on the decoder's web UI.

compatible_models.notes: All OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate models on firmware 2.0+. Some audio commands (mute, volume, AudioInput, AnalogPower, DisplayBtn, VolumeBtn, InputBtn) are Pro-only and silently no-op on R-Type units.

drivers.name: Extron SIS Protocol
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Extron products via the SIS (Simple Instruction Set) protocol. Covers crosspoint matrix switchers (DXP, CrossPoint), presentation switchers (IN Series), scalers (DSC, DVS), distribution amplifiers, and DSP products. Works over TCP (port 23) or RS-232 (9600 8N1).

help.overview: Universal control for Extron products using the SIS protocol. Works with 200+ products including crosspoint matrix switchers, presentation switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and DSPs.
help.setup: 1. Connect the Extron device to the network or via RS-232 (9600 8N1). 2. For TCP control, set the device's IP address and use port 23 (default). 3. Extron recommends a 100ms delay between commands (pre-configured).

compatible_models.notes: Any Extron product implementing the SIS protocol (~200 products).

drivers.name: Kramer Protocol 3000
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Kramer products via Protocol 3000 over TCP (port 5000). Covers matrix switchers (VS series), scalers (VP series), distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems.

help.overview: Controls Kramer matrix switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems via Protocol 3000. Common in corporate AV, education, and houses of worship.
help.setup:
1. Connect the switcher to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the IP address via the front panel menu or Kramer Network. 3. Enter the IP address and port 5000 (default) in the device config. 4. Machine number defaults to 01. Change it if multiple Kramer units
   share the same port.

drivers.name: Lightware LW3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lightware switchers and matrix routers via Protocol #3 (LW3) over TCP port 6107. Covers UCX, Taurus UCX, MMX2, MMX, and MX2M products. Provides video and audio crosspoint switching, mute, lock, HDCP, output 5V, embedded- audio mute, EDID switching, analog audio level/mute/balance, and CEC command sending.

help.overview: Lightware LW3 is the unified ASCII control protocol used across Lightware's matrix switchers, extenders, and modular routers. Commands target a tree of nodes (e.g. /V1/MEDIA/VIDEO/XP) using GET, SET, and CALL operations. The driver exposes the most-used runtime control surface: video and audio routing, mute, HDCP, output power, EDID, analog audio level, and CEC.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Lightware device to the network via Ethernet. 2. Confirm the device's IP address using LDC (Lightware Device Controller)
   or the front-panel display.
3. In LDC's Network tab, ensure the LW3 service on port 6107 is enabled
   and that authentication (IPLogin) is OFF — this driver does not
   authenticate.
4. Enter the IP address and port 6107 in the device config. 5. Use input/output port numbers as integers (I3 → input=3, O2 → output=2).
   Setting input=0 disconnects an output.
6. Polled state covers I1..I4 and O1..O4. Larger devices respond to
   routing commands on any valid port number.

compatible_models.notes: Any Lightware product that implements LW3 (most products since 2012). Polled state covers ports I1..I4 and O1..O4 — adequate for UCX, Taurus, and MMX2; commands accept any port number for larger MX2M frames.
